source: Post-war Iowa records (death, GAR, census, grave) — the survivor's trail
rationale: Alexander survived the war and moved to Iowa, so the identity-carrying spine shifts forward in time (V2 plan §4): death record, GAR, census, cemetery — not a KIA/burial record as for Henry.

records.name: Pocahontas County (Iowa) Civil War Soldiers Database — IAGenWeb (compiled by Linda Linn)
records.method: Direct fetch of the HTML table; located the Hubbell row.
records.verbatim_row: Hubbell, Alexander F. * @ doc | [U.S. Civil War Soldier Records and Profiles] Age at enlistment: 18; Enlistment Date: 21 Sep 1861; Rank at enlistment: Corporal; Enlistment Place: Champlain, NY; State Served: New York; Survived the War?: Yes; Enlisted in Company H, New York 60th Infantry Regiment on 30 Oct 1861; Promoted to Full Sergeant on 01 Oct 1862; Mustered out on 17 Jul 1865 at Alexandria, VA; Birth Date: abt 1843; Sources: New York: Report of the Adjutant-General | Marker: GAR star | Buried: Cedar twp., Fonda | DOB: 28 Mar 1844 | DOD: 7 Dec 1894

key_data.buried: Cedar Township, Fonda, Pocahontas County, Iowa
key_data.gar_marker: GAR star (Grand Army of the Republic — confirms veteran/GAR affiliation)

records.claude_reasoning: C4 (strong): DOB 1844-03-28 and burial Cedar twp. Fonda match the family genealogy exactly; pairs with the 60th NY Co. H service line. Resolves the family-internal death-date conflict toward DEC 7, 1894 — it carries the family's 'Dec 7' day with the '1894' year, implying the alternative 'Dec 7, 1899' is a year transcription error (the 1899 Iowa newspaper 'Hubbell' hits are all the unrelated F. M. Hubbell namesake). Verdict held at 'likely' (not 'confirmed') for the death date because this is a compiled database, not a contemporaneous obituary or the stone itself — confirmation handoff is the FindAGrave/WPA stone and the widow-pension filing date.

handoffs.item: WPA Grave Registration record for HUBBELL, Pocahontas County
handoffs.evidence: A 'HUBBELL' surname entry EXISTS in the Iowa WPA Grave Registration index for Pocahontas County (https://iagenweb.org/pocahontas/cemeteries/pocahontas-wpa.html), linking to https://iowawpagraves.org/index.php?last=HUBBELL&cid=76&lc=4 — but the detail page returned 403 and its death-date field could not be opened.
handoffs.value: Would confirm the stone-transcribed death date (1894 vs 1899).

handoffs.collections: 1870 + 1880 U.S. Federal (Dover Twp, Pocahontas Co.); 1885 + 1895 Iowa State Census; 1900 U.S. Federal.
handoffs.value: 1900 is a high-value disambiguator: if Alexander died in 1894, he should be ABSENT from 1900 and a widow-headed household for Lois + children (Frederick/Affa/Wolcott/Helen) should appear — independently corroborating a pre-1900 death.

handoffs.evidence: Cemetery confirmed to exist: https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery/2196697/cedar-township-cemetery ('1675 memorial records'). Individual memorial not retrievable by automation.
handoffs.value: Stone-transcribed death date + any linked Lois Wood Hubbell memorial.

confidence: external · n/a · likely (death date); definite (Iowa residence + GAR)
notes: The single most useful free post-war source was the IAGenWeb Pocahontas CW database. Cedar Cemetery transcription (iagenweb.org/pocahontas/cemeteries/cedar.htm) is a PARTIAL list and did NOT contain Hubbell (null, not absent).
